title.narrative: Provision of emergency Health Services for Drought-Affected Communities in Awdal (Zailac), Northwest Somaliland”:

description.narrative: ltpgtThe provision of emergency health services for drought-affected communities in Awdal (Zaila), the Northwest Somaliland project, is a seven-month project implemented by WAAPO with the support of UNOCHA/SFH under the health sector. The project is dedicated to supporting the most vulnerable communities affected by the drought. The core interventions will support health facilities: 4 fixed HFs 5 Mobile Teams in Zailac dritrict, Awdal. The skills and capacities of health staff at the regional, district, and village levels will be strengthened on key health-related topics. The project will reactivate 4 health facilities in Zailac district, namely ltbrgtZaylac, Toqoshi, lowyacado cabdiqadir health facilities by supporting and providing supplies and equipment necessary for the delivery of essential emergency Health services. As well as another 5 mobile health teams at the community-level hard-to-reach locations which incl. Geed had village, Jidhi village, Ashs ado village, sheikh aware village daba dilaac village." The Mobile team (MTs) will be attached to the fixed health facilities supported by the project and save the children funded facilities. ltspangtAt the community level, social mobilizers and community volunteers will also be mobilizing communities on health-related topics. UNOCHA will support the project through the SHF 2025 Reserve Allocation 2round. UNICEF and MoHD as direct partners with WAAPO will also expect to to provide relevant project supplies, mainly essential health and integrated nutrition and EPI supplies. WAAPO will work with all relevant project Clusters and Line-Ministries particularly MOH/MoPs to ensure effective coordination and efficient project services. The appeal letter was issued (April,2026.) From M,oP In Somaliland indicated that the current drought has left 691,850 individuals (115,308 households) in urgent need of assistance, without immediate intervention, the situation continues to deteriorate. The coastal and subcoastal areas such as Lughaya, Zeila, and Golis ranges of Borama and Baki are experiencing similar climate-induced challenges and humaniterain concern incl.
